- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce the forecast peak to avoid overshoot.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward correction — allow slight lagged rebound.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days trending down from high), model should not overcorrect upward.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in 2+ consecutive days, reduce next-day forecast by 1–2% to account for momentum decay.  
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating +/–0.5+), model should smooth forecasts — avoid sharp directional shifts.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.2–0.4), forecast should align with recent 7-day average, not 30-day trend.  
- If forecast is consistently 3–5% above true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias correction by 1–2% per day.  
- If forecast is consistently 3–5% below true outcome, apply upward bias correction by 1–2% per day.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., +3%+ per week), forecast should not lag by >2 days — adjust to match trend.  
- If sentiment is positive but price is falling, model should not assume continuation — expect mean reversion or short-term reversal.
